newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico livestock report, feeder export price - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Mexico livestock report, feeder export price - USDA.

text.p: USDA reported Monday that around 2,400 head were exported into the United States at four crossing points on Friday.
Through Santa Teresa, New Mexico, around 1,300 head were exported with feeder steers selling steady. "Trade moderate, demand goo," USDA said.
The bulk of supply consisted of steers weighing 600-650 lbs, priced at 68 cents/lb, it added.
Through Del Rio and Eagle Pass, Texas, around 450 head were exported although not enough head were sold form indicative market prices, USDA said.
Through Nogales, Arizona, around 650 head were exported with calves selling 2 to 3 cents/lb higher in active trade where demand was good.
Feeder steers weighing 300-400 lb sold at 76-86 cents/lb and those weighing 400-500 lb came in at between 68-76 cents/lb.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com))
